_readme: This is the SINGLE authoritative manifest of every backend runtime process Goat OS
deploys or intends to deploy from the goatos-backend image: what binary it runs, the
exact arguments it is invoked with, and what kind of process it is (long-running
'service', scheduled/one-shot 'job', or a documented not-yet-deployed future target).
Consumers (must not diverge from this file; add a new consumer here when you add one):
1. tools/agent-hooks/check-deployed-job-flags.mjs (`make deployed-job-flags-guard`)
cross-checks every infra/envs/{dev,stg}/cloud_run_jobs.tf job's command+args
against the matching entry here, checks every arg here is a flag the binary's
backend/cmd/<name>/*.go parser actually defines, and checks every binary here is
built by backend/Dockerfile.
2. tools/e2e/check-image-parity.mjs (`make e2e-parity`) runs every entry's exact
binary+args against the REAL built goatos-backend:e2e image (not `go run`).
3. deploy/e2e/docker-compose.e2e.yml wires the `kernel_worker` service entry's
command verbatim (kept in sync manually; e2e-parity/the guard fail loudly on drift).
4. infra/envs/{dev,stg}/cloud_run_jobs.tf and cloud_run_services.tf remain the actual
Terraform deployment; this file documents/validates them, it does not generate them.
KERN-001 (2026-07): obligation-sweeper's deployed job passed -project-calendar /
-project-vaccination-read-models, two flags retired from its flag parser when the
Calendar/vaccination screen projections were dropped (migration 000187). The job's
flag.Parse failed on every scheduled run and neither the sweeper's own operational work
nor its reminder/escalation sweep (-sweep-reminders/-sweep-escalations) ever ran, and
kernel-worker was never actually deployed anywhere despite existing fully built. Neither
failure mode is visible to `go build ./...` (Terraform args are plain strings) or to the
previous `go run`-based E2E (it never ran the built image with the deployed command).
This manifest plus the two checks above exist to make that class of drift a fast,
offline, deterministic failure instead of a silent production outage.
KERN-01 two-phase kernel-worker cutover (2026-07): the 7 environments.dev.jobs entries
flagged 'TRANSITIONAL legacy stage job' (domain-event-consumer, outbox-relay,
domain-event-processed-sweeper, generate-vaccination-obligations, inventory-batch-reconciler,
idempotency-key-sweeper, sop-review-fanout-retry) are retained ONLY for the parity-first
cutover to the consolidated kernel-worker SERVICE. In infra/envs/dev/cloud_run_jobs.tf
they are gated by var.retire_legacy_stage_jobs: phase 1 (flag=false) retains their definitions
the kernel-worker service for parity verification; phase 2 (flag=true) removes them once the
service is proven healthy. Staging completed the disposable cutover in 2026-07: it has no
scheduled stage jobs or partition maintainer; the analytics rollup remains a separately built
manual Cloud Run Job and is intentionally outside this backend-image manifest.

backend.notes: Default image for every entry below unless an entry sets "image": "migrate". Built by `make e2e-image-build`; this is local.backend_image in infra/envs/*/cloud_run_jobs.tf and cloud_run_services.tf.

migrate.e2e_tag: built inline by deploy/e2e/docker-compose.e2e.yml's migrate service (no standalone make target — it is small and only ever runs once per stack)
migrate.notes: This is local.migration_image in Terraform: a separate, smaller image containing only /app/bin/migrate + the migrations directory. Never merged into the backend image.

services.name: api
services.notes: No command/args override in Terraform: infra/envs/{dev,stg}/cloud_run_services.tf (stg) and the dev API service run the image's Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT as-is.

services.name: mcp
services.health_signal: GET /readyz returns 200 when MESHA_MCP_UPSTREAM_URL or MESHA_MCP_UPSTREAM_ASK_URL is configured
services.notes: External leadership-assistant MCP facade for Claude, Codex, and ChatGPT-style clients. Terraform runs /app/bin/mcp from the backend image and proxies tool calls to goatos-api-stg /ceo-ai/ask so the API remains authoritative for auth, tenant scope, ceo_internal role, audit, and read-only business access.

services.name: kernel_worker
services.health_signal: process stays running (no restarts); structured logs kernel_worker_starting then per-cadence stage logs (fast/operational/generation/housekeeping) and, when Pub/Sub is configured, no domain_consumer_disabled log
services.notes: Consolidated long-running kernel worker (backend/cmd/kernel-worker/main.go, backend/internal/kernelstages, backend/internal/platform/worker; built by backend/Dockerfile). Deployed as a Cloud Run SERVICE (min=2/max=2, CPU always-on, /readyz+/livez probes) in dev and stg via infra/envs/{dev,stg}/cloud_run_worker.tf, replacing the retired per-stage scheduled jobs. command+args here (/app/bin/kernel-worker -timeout=0s) are reconciled bidirectionally against those Terraform services by check-deployed-job-flags.mjs, and exercised by deploy/e2e/docker-compose.e2e.yml + make e2e-parity/e2e-smoke.

jobs.name: migrate
jobs.schedule: deploy-time (run once per release, not scheduled)
jobs.notes: Deployed from local.migration_image (backend/Dockerfile.migrate), a SEPARATE image from local.backend_image/goatos-backend:e2e — see the top-level images.migrate entry. tools/agent-hooks/check-deployed-job-flags.mjs still validates its binary/flags (it unions binaries across every backend/Dockerfile*); make e2e-parity skips the goatos-backend:e2e binary-existence check for it and instead relies on deploy/e2e/docker-compose.e2e.yml's migrate service, which builds Dockerfile.migrate and actually runs this exact binary+args against real Postgres.

jobs.name: domain_event_consumer
jobs.notes: TRANSITIONAL legacy stage job — retained for the two-phase kernel-worker cutover (see _readme). Gated in Terraform by var.retire_legacy_stage_jobs; remove when the flag flips true (phase 2).

jobs.name: herd_signals_partition_maintenance
jobs.health_signal: exit code 0; partitions_created/partitions_dropped counters emitted per run — a sustained zero created is the failure to watch, because the runway silently expiring sends every new packet to the DEFAULT partition and kills pruning

jobs.name: migrate
jobs.schedule: deploy-time (run once per release, not scheduled)
jobs.notes: Deployed from local.migration_image (backend/Dockerfile.migrate), a SEPARATE image from local.backend_image/goatos-backend:e2e — see the top-level images.migrate entry. tools/agent-hooks/check-deployed-job-flags.mjs still validates its binary/flags (it unions binaries across every backend/Dockerfile*); make e2e-parity skips the goatos-backend:e2e binary-existence check for it and instead relies on deploy/e2e/docker-compose.e2e.yml's migrate service, which builds Dockerfile.migrate and actually runs this exact binary+args against real Postgres.

jobs.name: feed_direction_issue
jobs.health_signal: exit code 0; feed_direction_issues row in state 'issued' for feed_day = as-of + 1
jobs.notes: ONE job, TWO scheduler triggers. The command self-gates on the authored clock (app/lifecycle_schedule.go: asOf.Before(issueAt) -> no-op), so the 07:00 wake-up issues normal and skips experiment, and the 14:00 wake-up issues experiment and no-ops on the already-issued normal. Freezing is the point: until a sheet is issued the API regenerates it live on every read and an authorized shifting moves quantities the operator has already packed against.

jobs.name: feed_direction_amend
jobs.health_signal: exit code 0; issue in state 'amended' (or an unchanged no-op that still stamped amended_at)

jobs.name: feed_direction_lock
jobs.notes: 15:30, not 15:45: migration 000104 aligned transport_time with the hard 15:30 gate in MaterializeTransportTasks so the sheet locks exactly when transport is raised.

e2e.notes: The compose stack runs the api service entry and the kernel_worker service entry from THIS manifest's services[] list, off the real built image — no `go run`, no mounted shell script. Phase-2 adds business-chain assertions (obligation -> batch -> SOP -> notification) on top of this skeleton; see the seam comment in the compose file.

_readme: Documented NOT-YET-DEPLOYED future targets (the third process category named in the top _readme).
A binary listed here is built by backend/Dockerfile and production-ready, but is not yet wired into
infra/envs/{dev,stg}/cloud_run_jobs.tf, so it deliberately does NOT live under environments.*.jobs:
check-deployed-job-flags.mjs asserts bidirectional TF<->manifest parity for env jobs, and claiming a
job is deployed while no Terraform creates it would be a false-green. To promote one, move its entry
into environments.<env>.jobs and add the matching google_cloud_run_v2_job + Cloud Scheduler blocks
in the SAME change -- and put them in the file that environment's tf_file names, because the guard
reads exactly that one file.
Feed Direction issuance was promoted to environments.stg.jobs on 2026-08-07 (normal direction 07:00,
experiment 14:00, correction 14:00, transport 15:30 Asia/Kolkata; each run acts on
feed_day = as-of + 1). It is still absent from environments.dev.jobs -- dev has no feed data to issue.
